The main takeaway from our work is that
the Messinian salinity crisis (MSC) is a consequence of a major environmental change in the Mediterranean, and not of the eustatic sea-level fall.

the Tortonian–Early Messinian carbonate complexes of the western and the central Mediterranean are the product of a major transgressive–regressive cycle, which is recorded on the different platforms by two major sedimentary cycles, and by two major index surfaces.

the Messinian carbonate complexes in the western and southern Mediterranean are the result of a complex interplay of tectonics, eustasy and climate, which resulted in a variety of depositional settings.
